QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_40

question.text: 'Yamuna Category II AIF' holds preference shares with 'protective provisions'. Which of the following corporate actions typically falls under these provisions?

answer.text: Routine hiring of a junior marketing executive
Modification to the Memorandum or Articles of Association, corporate restructuring, dividend declaration, redemption of shares, or establishing a new option plan

explanation.text: The Logic: Protective provisions give preferred stockholders (generally minority/preference holders) the ability to approve important corporate decisions: MOA/AOA modification, corporate restructuring/M&A, dividend to common/preferred, redemption of shares, new option plans, board-size changes, dissolution. Routine operating matters are OUT of scope. The Trap: Junior hires, office supplies, utility bills are not 'material corporate actions' — they don't need preferred-holder consent. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests protective provisions. Overlaps with affirmative-rights list; 'protective' is the term preferred in US-style VC docs, 'affirmative' in Indian practice — scope is similar. Manager's Pro-Tip: In drafting, include a 'basket threshold' (e.g., capital expenditure > INR 10 crore, related-party transactions > INR 1 crore) so routine business doesn't get choked by veto approvals.
